title: Electric Field and Mean Inner Potential in BSCCO Below Tc Using a Liquid Helium Holder, Lorentz 4D-STEM and Electron Holography
content: Recently a profound connection between the volume average electrostatic potentials (MIP) [1] and superconductivity was identified by J. E. Hirsch [2]. The theory proposed by the author suggests that the possible expansion of electron orbitals and the spatial extent of electronic wavefunctions in the superconducting state cause charge asymmetry within the crystal interior. This charge asymmetry that occurs in the superconducting state can lead to negative charge expulsion to the surface and to an increased MIP value at sufficiently low temperatures, in our case we used the Gatan liquid Helium holder at 30 Kelvin which is below the superconducting critical temperature (Tc) [2]. However, to date, according to our understanding there has been no experimental report of any measured changes in the MIP of materials becoming superconducting in electron microscopy experiments as well no evidence for surface effect caused by this negative charge expulsion to the surface.
